title: Tale of Mohsin and Musa
summary: In Baghdad lived two cousins: Mohsin (The Benevolent) and Musa (The Schemer). Their father left them an equal inheritance of five thousan...
full_text:
In Baghdad lived two cousins: Mohsin (The Benevolent) and Musa (The Schemer). Their father left them an equal inheritance of five thousand gold dinars each.

Mohsin invested his share in honest trade, established a bakery that provided free bread to widows and orphans, and treated his apprentices with fatherly affection.
Musa, on the other hand, hoarded his gold in iron chests, lent money at extortionate interest, and sneered at Mohsin's charity:
'Thou art a fool, Mohsin! Bread given away is gold drowned in the river. Wealth is meant to be hoarded, not scattered!'

Years passed. A terrible fire broke out in the merchant quarter of Baghdad. Musa's fortified warehouse, locked with triple bolts, trapped its own heat, and all his silks, tapestries, and ledgers burned to fine ash! Musa was left penniless, weeping in the street.

Hearing of his cousin's ruin, Mohsin did not utter a single word of reproach.
He went immediately to Musa, embraced him warmly, took him to his own home, clothed him in fine wool robes, and divided his remaining trading stock equally with him, saying:
'Brother, wealth is a loan from heaven. When thine is lost, mine is thine. Take half of my business, and let us rebuild together.'

Musa wept bitter tears of remorse. His heart of stone broke under the warmth of Mohsin's unconditional generosity.
'O Mohsin,' he sobbed, 'for twenty years I mocked thy charity, believing myself wise. Today I see that the gold I hoarded burned in an hour, but the kindness thou didst scatter among the people built a fortress of love that no fire can touch.'

Musa reformed his ways completely, becoming Mohsin's faithful partner in both commerce and philanthropy. Their business flourished tenfold, proving that generous charity is the only investment that never fails.
moral: Selfless generosity and trust in divine providence outlast envious schemes, yielding enduring honor.
